evidence.observation: The plan says: '**GO2-C1** a proposal of four operations, one of which the candidate validation refuses: the preview names all four, three `admitted` and one refused with its verdict, exit 3' and 'A refusal that names no element stays a refusal of the whole proposal and the preview says so in one row.' In the code, EvolutionPreview (evolve/models.py:1036-1055) requires verbalization, validation: ValidationEvidence, affected_references, breaking and blast_radius. All of them are built from the loaded candidate (_validated_candidate, service.py:1507-1518). A candidate that fails validation raises EvolutionError inside _load_model_document (service.py:294-295), and no preview exists. policy_issues work today only because the candidate has already validated by then (service.py:1534-1537).

concerns.recommendation: Add a decision on what document carries the outcomes of a refused proposal. Either use a refusal report separate from EvolutionPreview, or make the candidate-derived preview fields optional. Say what apply does with that document, and add a criterion that apply refuses it.
concerns.title: GO2-C1 needs a preview of a candidate that fails validation, and the preview model cannot hold one

evidence.observation: The plan says: '**GO2-C3** a proposal admitted today has every operation `admitted` and every other preview field byte-identical, apart from the schema version', 'The preview's schema version moves', D2 '(a) A new `operation_outcomes` list in the preview, under a new preview schema version', and R0.3 'a proposal admitted today has every other field unchanged'. In the code, _bindings_match refuses a preview whose version differs from its proposal's ('preview and proposal versions must match', evolve/models.py:1096-1097), and preview() refuses any proposal that is not at EVOLUTION_SCHEMA_VERSION (service.py:1557-1561). Moving the preview version therefore moves the proposal version, and every v3 proposal a host holds is refused. proposal_sha256 is canonical_sha256 over the proposal (models.py:720-721), and preview_sha256 binds the whole body (models.py:1160-1162), so both digests change and GO2-C3 fails. Precedent at models.py:867-875: optional fields omitted when unset kept the bytes and preview_sha256 with no version move.

concerns.recommendation: Either add operation_outcomes under the _OPTIONAL_PREVIEW_FIELDS omit-when-unset rule without moving the version, or decouple the preview version from the proposal version in a stated decision. Restate GO2-C3 to exclude the digests that must change, and record in §5 the cost of the version move for v3 proposals.
concerns.title: GO2-C3 cannot hold: moving the preview schema version moves the proposal version and changes every digest

evidence.observation: The plan says: '**GO5-C2** a round that proposes nothing and a round whose proposals all map onto existing elements give different summaries' and 'GND computes the summary from the proposal and its preview ... The host supplies what it dropped before the proposal as an input file'. In the code, EvolutionProposal.operations is Field(min_length=1) (evolve/models.py:647-651), so a round that proposes nothing has no proposal or preview to summarize. A reply that only reuses existing ids and adds no rows (the GO4 rule) produces no operation either. D4(a)'s input file lists drops, not reuses, and the shape report (H18) covers only added fact types. No input named in the plan tells the two rounds apart, and telling them apart is the point of #227.

concerns.recommendation: Define the source of 'mapped onto existing elements', for example by having the host file also list reused ids, or by having the summary read the reply. Define the summary for a round with no proposal. Build GO5-C2's two fixtures so they differ only in that input.
concerns.title: GO5-C2 cannot be met: an empty round has no proposal, and reused elements leave no operation

evidence.observation: D1 proposes '(a) ... each tied to its operation where the refusal names an element' and '(a). A refusal that names no element stays a whole-proposal refusal and says so'. GO2-C2 says '**GO2-C2** one case per verdict word, each reachable with a committed fixture', and the verdict list includes `refused-by-d12`. In the code, every refusal in _enforce_d12 (service.py:428-477) names no element, for example 'new induced constraints must be proposed/deontic (D-12)', and the loop raises at the first failing constraint. _model_warnings also raises on layer-1 issues before layer 2 runs (model/__init__.py:302-304). Under D1(a), then, `refused-by-d12` can never be a per-operation verdict. An operation marked `admitted` after one pass may also hide a refusal that the first one masked, so GO3-C1 holds only for fixtures with a single fault.

concerns.recommendation: State in GO2 that the D-12 gate and candidate validation will collect every refusal with its host or locator, keeping today's first message and exit for the whole-proposal path. Otherwise, define `admitted` as 'no refusal found in this pass' and have the narrowed proposal re-previewed. Add a fixture with two faults in two different operations.
concerns.title: Under D1(a) no D-12 refusal can be tied to an operation, and a single pass cannot establish `admitted`

evidence.observation: The plan says: '**GO3-C3** ... applying the original preview after narrowing is refused as any stale preview is', and §6 says 'and the original preview stale'. GO3 is a library function that returns a new proposal and writes nothing (§2, D5 a). Apply refuses a preview as stale only when the live model's sha differs from preview.before_model.sha256 (service.py:2187-2191; 'stale' maps to exit 11, cli_service.py:283-334). After narrowing alone the model has not changed. If apply refuses the original preview, it does so by re-running validation and policy (service.py:2142-2153, :2203-2210), and that refusal has a different message and exit.

concerns.recommendation: Split GO3-C3 into two cases. First, before the narrowed proposal is applied, apply refuses the original preview through revalidation, with today's message and exit. Second, after the narrowed proposal is applied, apply refuses the original preview as a stale model CAS, exit 11.
concerns.title: GO3-C3 expects the original preview to go stale, but narrowing changes no model bytes

evidence.location: §2 GO1; §1 H5; GO1 spec lines 114-117 and T5 line 170
evidence.observation: The plan says the parse returns 'the document it already built for the same bytes and the same reader', and H5 says 'reads `source` only for its suffix (`.json` selects the strict JSON reader) ... For the same bytes and the same reader it returns equal documents'. Spec lines 114-117 define the reader as 'the value of the parser's own reader test ... (`_parsing.py:37`: the `.json` suffix, or text that starts with `{`)'. But _parsing.py:46-50 refuse a JSONDecodeError only under a .json suffix and otherwise fall back to YAML. Bytes like '{version: 5, ...}' are refused under model.orm.json, parse under model.orm.yaml, and share that key. In apply, _parse_model_text parses the current text under 'model.orm.yaml' (service.py:344, called at :2145) before _load_model_document reads the same bytes under the workspace name (:2203). With a .json workspace and a hand-built preview, the cached YAML document would be returned, and today's 'model JSON input refused' would disappear, against R0.2 and R0.3. Spec T5 catches this only if its bytes do not start with '{'.

concerns.recommendation: Key the cache on (sha256, Path(source).suffix == '.json'); that is the only way source changes a successful parse. Make T5 use YAML-flow bytes that start with '{' under both names, and expect the .json refusal even after the .yaml parse succeeded.
concerns.title: GO1's cache key treats the strict JSON reader and the JSON-then-YAML fallback as one reader

evidence.location: §3 table GO4 and GO5 rows; §3 Order; H21
evidence.observation: The GO5 row needs only 'GO2 merged into the branch; D4 ruled', yet it changes '`unattended-growth.md`'. The GO4 row needs 'VG2 and VG5 of reviewed-vocabulary-growth merged or not started (H21)'. Order: 'GO4 at any point after its ruling'. H21: 'VG1, then GO1, then VG2–VG5, then GO2–GO5'. GO2's start condition covers only VG2 and VG4, so GO5 can start while VG5 still has unattended-growth.md open. That is the two-writer case §6 claims to control. The 'or not started' clauses and 'any point' also let GO2 or GO4 land ahead of VG2–VG5, contrary to H21.

concerns.recommendation: Give GO5 the 'VG2 and VG5 merged' condition that GO4 has. Either drop 'or not started' and 'any point', or state that they amend the order H21 cites from the roadmap.
concerns.title: GO5 edits unattended-growth.md without the VG5 start condition, and GO4's timing contradicts H21's order

evidence.location: §4 GO1 row; §9 GO1 lane; Provenance lines 22-26
evidence.observation: The plan says: '**Which gate is which:** C1 to C4 read no clock and are the required regression gates; C5 compares two runs on one machine'. Yet the §9 GO1 lane runs `tests/test_go1_evolve_parse_once.py` and expects exit 0. The Provenance paragraph says: 'by up to 77 % for the sub-second and one-second timings at 604'. GO1 spec lines 155 and 173 put T8 (the C5 ratio) in that same file in the 'default lane'. T8 makes four apply runs at 604 object types, about 18 s by H6's figures. A scoped apply there takes about 2 s, inside the 77 % band, so a loaded runner can fail a lane the plan calls clock-free.

concerns.recommendation: Put the C5 test behind a marker excluded from the default and focused lanes, or record it as C6 is recorded. Keep C1's parse count as the regression gate, and say so in §4 and §9.
concerns.title: GO1-C5's timed ratio runs in the required GO1 lane, though §4 says only C1–C4 are required

summary: GO1 holds up against the code. Every cited line in src/gnd matches this checkout, and the 22 and 6 parse counts agree with the call sites. No caller in evolve/service.py, model/__init__.py or model/_includes.py writes into the parsed document: compose and _merge clone, json_document rebuilds, and _finish_model takes shallow copies. R0.2 holds. GO1's one real defect is that its cache key treats the strict JSON reader and the JSON-then-YAML fallback as the same reader. GO2, GO3 and GO5 cannot be built or tested as written. GO2-C1 needs a preview of an invalid candidate, which the preview model cannot hold. GO2-C3 cannot hold once the schema version moves. Under D1(a), no D-12 refusal can be tied to an operation. GO3-C3 expects a stale preview that narrowing never creates. GO5-C2 has nothing to tell an empty round from a covered one. The one-writer order also leaves a gap: GO5 can edit unattended-growth.md while VG5 still has it open.
